title: DIY Shopify or hire a designer: what you save and risk
excerpt: Hire a Shopify designer or DIY? What each route costs in Canada in dollars and hours, the setup tasks people get wrong, and a rule based on catalogue size.
keywords: hire Shopify designer vs DIY, Shopify setup service cost, Shopify expert price Canada, build Shopify store yourself, Shopify setup cost Canada
cover_title: Shopify: Build It or Hire It?
intro_html:
You started a Shopify trial, picked a theme, added three products, and then hit the settings pages: shipping, taxes, policies, payments. Now you are wondering whether to push through on your own or pay someone to finish it properly.

I run my own online store and build them for clients, so I see both sides. This post puts numbers on each route using prices and time estimates published in 2026, all checked on October 5, 2026, then lists the setup tasks that most often go wrong and a simple way to decide.

sections.heading: What DIY costs: a few dollars and a lot of hours
sections.body_html:
In money, building it yourself is close to free at the start. Shopify's Canadian pricing page offers three days free and then $1 a month for three months. After that, Basic is $49 CAD a month paid monthly or $37 paid yearly, and Shopify says there are no setup fees on any plan. A marketplace for Shopify freelancers, shopexperts, puts the cash cost of a DIY setup at $0 to $200.

The real cost is time. A per-task estimate from Do Dropshipping, updated in July 2026, puts a store at 19 to 54 hours: 6 to 22 hours on design, 3 to 13 adding products, 2 to 5 on technical configuration, and the rest on the plan, apps and suppliers.

Put a price on those hours. This part is my arithmetic, not a published figure: if an hour of your time is worth $40 to the business, 19 to 54 hours is $760 to $2,160. At $75 an hour it is $1,425 to $4,050. If you are not yet trading and your evenings are free, the honest figure may be zero.
sections.takeaway: Before you compare quotes, write down what an hour of your time is worth and multiply it by 20 and by 50. That range is your true DIY price.

sections.heading: What hiring costs in Canada
sections.body_html:
Published prices for a small-store setup cluster lower than the big agency figures suggest.

  • A Toronto designer. Elevate Web Design (June 2026) says a typical Toronto small-business ecommerce site runs roughly $2,000 to $8,000 to build, and lists its own fixed packages at $599, $1,995 and $2,995 and up.
  • An offshore team selling to Canada. Codingclave, based in Lucknow, India, prices a starter assisted setup at CAD 1,500 to 4,000 over one to two weeks, and puts Canadian Shopify freelancers at CAD 70 to 130 an hour.
  • A freelancer marketplace. shopexperts gives $500 to $2,500 for a basic freelancer setup under 100 products and $2,500 to $10,000 for 100 to 1,000 products. The page does not state a currency.
  • Shopify's own directory. The Partner Directory showed 4,763 partners for store build or redesign on October 5, 2026, with first-page starting prices from $100 to $10,000 USD and a filter for partners in Canada.
  • Agency-style guides. WebDesignGuide (updated June 2026) puts a standard Shopify or WooCommerce build at CA$5,000 to $15,000.

For comparison, our own ecommerce build at Nova Toronto is $2,000 plus applicable tax, on Shopify or WooCommerce.
sections.takeaway: For a store under 100 products, expect real Canadian quotes between about $600 and $4,000. If a quote is far above that, ask what custom work justifies it; if it is far below, ask who does the work and what is left out.

sections.heading: The setup tasks people get wrong
sections.body_html:
Design is the part everyone worries about. The expensive mistakes are in settings.

Taxes. Shopify's Canadian tax setup page says a Canada-based store generally needs a GST/HST account once taxable revenue passes $30,000 CAD over the past four completed calendar quarters or within the current quarter. Collection is something you switch on, region by region, under Settings, then Taxes and duties. Shopify is also clear that charging the right rates and filing correctly is your responsibility, not the platform's. This is a summary, not tax advice; confirm your own position with an accountant.

Shipping. Shopify's shipping rates page describes three choices: flat rates you set, free shipping, or rates calculated by a carrier. It also notes that a country has to be in an active market before you can sell to it.

Policies. The store policies page lists six, including return, privacy, shipping and terms of service, and offers templates for English checkouts. They are linked automatically in your checkout footer, and Shopify reminds you that you are responsible for following whatever you publish. A pasted template promising 30-day returns is a promise.

Testing. Shopify's test orders page recommends placing at least one test order to confirm checkout, shipping, email notifications and taxes all behave. It also warns that customers cannot place live orders while your payment provider is in test mode, so switch it back.
sections.takeaway: Whichever route you choose, place a test order to an Ontario address and to one other province before launch, and read the tax line, shipping charge and confirmation email as a customer would.

sections.heading: What a setup service should hand over
sections.body_html:
shopexperts lists what the word setup should cover: admin configuration, theme installation and customization, product catalogue setup, payment gateway, shipping configuration, apps and integrations, and quality checks before launch.

The same shopexperts guide names the usual disappointments: template work sold as custom design, subcontracting that was never disclosed, vague scope that grows, and a monthly retainer made a condition of the setup.

So get these in writing before you pay a deposit:

  • How many products will be loaded, and who supplies photos and descriptions
  • Who configures taxes and shipping, and for which provinces and countries
  • That the store, domain and theme licence sit in your own Shopify account, with you as owner
  • A recorded walkthrough or short training session so you can add products yourself
  • What support is included after launch, for how long, and what it costs after that
  • Who does the work
sections.takeaway: A good setup ends with you able to run the store without the person who built it. If a quote does not mention ownership and training, ask before you sign.

sections.heading: A simple rule based on catalogue size
sections.body_html:
This is my rule of thumb from building and running stores. The thresholds are judgment, not data.

  • Under about 25 products: build it yourself. The catalogue work is a weekend, a free theme is enough, and the hours teach you the admin you will use every day. Put the saved money into stock and photos.
  • 25 to 100 products: it depends on your hours. Product entry alone moves toward the top of that 3 to 13 hour range, and variants, collections and shipping rules multiply. If your DIY price from the first section comes out above the quote, hire. A middle path is to do the products yourself and pay a freelancer by the hour to check taxes, shipping and checkout.
  • 100 or more products, or a move from another platform: hire. Bulk imports, redirects and inventory are easy to get wrong and slow to fix.

Who should not hire anyone yet: a business still testing whether the product sells. Run the $1 months, list a handful of items, and find out. For the running costs once you are live, see what a Shopify store costs in Canada in year one.
sections.takeaway: Count your products and price your hours. Small catalogue and spare evenings: do it yourself. Large catalogue or a paying day job: the fee is usually the cheaper option.

bottom_line_html:
DIY costs almost nothing in cash and roughly 19 to 54 hours of your time. Hiring for a small store costs about $600 to $4,000 in Canada on published prices and takes one to three weeks. The saving from DIY is real when your catalogue is small and your time is free. The risk is in the tax, shipping and policy settings, which no theme fixes for you.

If you would rather hand it over, our ecommerce website build is $2,000 plus applicable tax on Shopify or WooCommerce. If you are doing it yourself, the free AI course for beginners covers writing product copy and making visuals with free tools. Still undecided? Book a free consultation and bring your product count and launch date.

faq.q: How much does it cost to hire someone to set up a Shopify store in Canada?
faq.a: Published 2026 prices for a small store run from about $600 to $4,000 CAD. Elevate Web Design in Toronto lists packages at $599, $1,995 and $2,995 and up; Codingclave prices a starter assisted setup at CAD 1,500 to 4,000. Agency-style guides quote $5,000 to $15,000 for a standard build. Nova Toronto's ecommerce build is $2,000 plus applicable tax.

faq.q: How long does it take to set up a Shopify store yourself?
faq.a: One per-task estimate, updated in July 2026, puts it at 19 to 54 hours: 6 to 22 on design, 3 to 13 adding products, 2 to 5 on technical configuration and the rest on plan, apps and suppliers. A hired small-store setup is typically quoted at one to three weeks.

faq.q: Can I build a Shopify store myself with no experience?
faq.a: Yes, for a small catalogue. Shopify offers three days free and then $1 a month for three months, with no setup fees, so a first attempt costs very little. The parts beginners most often get wrong are tax collection, shipping rates and store policies, so place a test order before you launch.

faq.q: What should a Shopify setup service include?
faq.a: At minimum: admin configuration, theme installation and customization, products loaded, payment gateway, shipping, tax settings, key apps and a pre-launch test. Get in writing how many products are loaded, that the store is in your own Shopify account, what training you receive and what support follows launch.
